chapter: Learning the drums and early influences
title: Stealing from other drummers and the first beats he played
summary: Crawford says he learned by watching, played four on the bass drum with press rolls, and loves his drums.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: No, thank you. So like -- so now, when you started playing -- what I mean is like, when you -- when you started playing with Luceford Tunsford's band in high school --
I didn't have no musical knowledge of drumming or just on what I could see from other drummers and pick up. Oh, yes, I was a stealer.
It had to be because I didn't have no education on drums, and I enjoyed my -- I enjoy my drums. I love my drums. I certainly do. I have a set sitting in the sun parlor now,

sits there. We put it out there. I didn't want to put it on my clean rugs. You know, you never know what happens. I have -- have them sitting up in here most of the time. I've got about three or four outfits out there in the garage, in the basement. Yeah, I love my drums.
So now, what -- now, when you started playing in high school, what kinds of beats did you have to play? I mean would you -- were you --
Four-four (Inaudible) up on a bass drum, up on a snare drum? We used to -- have a little lick, we used to roll like on it. S-s-sh-ump-s-s-sh-ump, and then we used a cymbal.
Oh, we're going to get to him. I know about him. Now, you say you were playing -- say you would be playing four quarter notes on the bass drum?
You were playing four quarter notes on the bass drum? And you would be playing --
Press roll, that's it. You're right. You're a drummer.
Yeah. And then finally we went to the cymbal up on the stands.
